CANDU-Style Reactor Core Monitor & SCRAM Simulator

A working bench model of a CANDU shutdown system. It monitors core temperature, trips automatically, and blocks unsafe resets.

5 Hzcontrol loop
>80%SCRAM trip
±0.5 °Caccuracy
  • Arduino Uno R3 with an NTC thermistor, servo-driven control rod, relay module, and 16×2 LCD.
  • Mounted everything on a plywood base with a 3D-printed servo bracket, a clear acrylic tube around the simulated core and control rod, and an indicator panel with SCRAM, CAUTION, and NORMAL LEDs and a reset button.
  • Three-state logic (NORMAL, CAUTION, SCRAM). On a trip the rod inserts and a relay simulates emergency core cooling.
  • Two-condition reset interlock (core under 55% and operator confirmation), modelled on reactor permissive logic.
  • Thermistor calibrated with the Steinhart-Hart equation, with documentation written for non-technical readers.

What it does

The simulator works like a small-scale reactor safety system. A thermistor reads the “core” temperature five times a second, and the Arduino shows the reading and the current state on the LCD. If the temperature passes the trip point, the servo drives the control rod in and a relay switches on to simulate emergency cooling. The system will not reset until the core cools below 55% and an operator confirms, the same way real shutdown systems prevent an unsafe restart.

Cable-Driven Robotic Arm

A motorized arm that raises and lowers a 3D-printed support around a pivot using a gear motor, cable spool, and actuation cable.

  • Designed the mechanical structure: a rigid black main frame and an orange support arm joined at a bolted pivot, with mounting slots and adjustable securing straps.
  • Built a cable-drive actuation system in which a gear motor winds an actuation cable onto a spool to rotate the support arm about the pivot.
  • Wired the motor to a control board with a power switch, adjustment knob, and digital display for operator control.
  • Assembled, tested, and adjusted the mechanism for smooth, controlled raising and lowering.

What it does

The arm works like a motorized hinge. When the motor runs, it winds the actuation cable onto the spool, which pulls the orange support upward around the pivot bolt. Letting the cable back out lowers the support in a controlled way. The control board’s switch, knob, and display let the operator run and adjust the motor, while the straps hold the device securely in place.

RC Car: CAD Model, Build & Drive Control

A remote-controlled car taken through the full cycle: a complete SolidWorks model, a hands-on build, and drive and steering code I wrote myself.

  • Modelled the whole car as a SolidWorks assembly (chassis, drivetrain, steering linkage, and electronics layout) before any physical work began.
  • Used the model to check fit, clearances, and packaging and to plan wiring and mounts, catching problems in CAD instead of on the bench.
  • Built the car from a kit: mounted the rear drive motor and front steering assembly, installed the control circuit board and switch board, and routed and secured the wiring across the chassis.
  • Programmed throttle, direction, and steering control, then tuned it over repeated test drives until it drove reliably.

What it does

The RC car is a remote-controlled vehicle that I modelled, built, and programmed. Before the build, a full SolidWorks assembly let me check how every part fit together and plan where the electronics and wiring would go. On the finished car, my code reads the remote's input and turns it into motor speed, direction, and steering. Test drives showed me what to adjust until the car drove smoothly and responded reliably.

TrackItLive Smart Ring & Companion App

A wearable fitness ring with a custom SolidWorks enclosure, a manufactured prototype, and a phone app for activity, nutrition, and biometrics.

  • Designed the ring enclosure in SolidWorks over multiple revisions for wearability, durability, and internal component fit.
  • Produced manufacturer-ready drawings and worked directly with a third-party manufacturer to fabricate the prototype.
  • Built the companion app in Expo / React Native with a custom Bluetooth Low Energy driver for the ring's sensor module, cross-checked against the manufacturer's SDK.
  • App features include photo-based meal logging, workout and weight tracking, and calorie-goal recommendations.

What it does

TrackItLive is a smart ring and phone app that work together to track health and fitness. The ring sits in a custom enclosure I designed to be comfortable, durable, and sized around its internal electronics. It sends biometric data to the app over Bluetooth Low Energy. The app combines that data with logged meals, workouts, and weight to recommend a daily calorie goal.
